title: Collection Keeper Checkpoint
intro: Lists, tuples and dictionaries all hold many values at once, and each one is good at a different job. Eleven rounds covering all three. Get them right on the first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.explain: Lists count from 0, so fruits[0] is the first item.

rounds.prompt: Negative indexes count back from the end. What prints?
rounds.explain: Index -1 is the last item, -2 is the one before it, and so on. It saves working out len(fruits) - 1 yourself.

rounds.prompt: This stops with an IndexError. The list has 3 items. Pick the fix.
options: Use a valid index such as colors[2]
Change the list into a tuple
rounds.explain: Three items use the indexes 0, 1 and 2. The last index is always the length minus one, so 3 is already past the end.

rounds.prompt: What is the length after this runs?
rounds.explain: .append() puts one item on the end, so a list of two becomes a list of three.

rounds.prompt: A for loop can walk through a list directly. What does this print?
rounds.explain: Looping over a list hands you the items themselves, one per turn. No indexes needed.

rounds.prompt: Which collection cannot be changed after you make it?
rounds.explain: A tuple is locked once created, which is exactly why you use one for values that should never move.

rounds.prompt: This crashes. Pick the fix that keeps the append working.
options: Make sizes a list with square brackets
Remove the quotes around the items
rounds.explain: A tuple has no .append() at all. If the collection needs to grow, it should have been a list from the start.
A dictionary looks a value up by its key, not by a position. The key "Mia" points at 11.

rounds.prompt: The key is not in the dictionary. What happens?
options: It adds Mia to the dictionary
rounds.explain: Reading a missing key is an error. ages.get("Mia") is the version that hands back None instead of crashing.

rounds.prompt: Match each collection or piece of syntax to what it is for.

pairs.right: A dictionary, looked up by key
How many items are in it
Add one item to the end of a list
Read a key without risking a crash

rounds.explain: The three bracket types are the three collections, and the three tools are the ones you reach for most: measure it, grow it, or read from it safely.

rounds.prompt: Build a list of two pets, add a third, then print how many there are.
rounds.explain: The list has to exist before you can append to it, and len() has to come after the append or it would report the old count.
